_what: Receipt for the two G6 facts analyze.py cannot observe about its own output, plus the archive identifier. Every value was measured by the command named beside it; none is asserted. It is bound to the run by run_commit and protocol_sha256 and is rejected whole if either fails to match. It lives OUTSIDE results/ on purpose: checksums.sha256 hashes results/, so a receipt kept there would be hashed by the very manifest whose verification it reports.
_run_commit: The commit the DATA were produced at, as raw/environment.json records it: the source-only freeze of protocol 3.0.0 and release 2.2.0. Later commits correct analysis and tooling defects and cannot reach the raw draws, which were already on disk.
_make_verify: MEASURED, twice. In the working tree at commit 00dbcce: raw/raw_checksums.sha256 ok, checksums.sha256 ok, exit 0. And from a fresh extraction of the archive below, where it is the check G6 actually asks for: `tools/verify_release.py` reported PASS on 'experiment checksum manifests verify'. analyze.py also verifies both manifests itself and the live measurement governs; this value agrees with it.
_make_reverify: MEASURED, twice. In the working tree at commit 00dbcce: 'every derived artifact regenerated byte for byte', exit 0. And from the fresh extraction: PASS on 'derived artifacts regenerate byte-identically'. Both runs used the widened target of commit 3161040, which diffs figures/ as well as results/ -- before that it regenerated the figures and compared only the results, so a figure that failed to reproduce would have gone unnoticed while invalidating the manifest that hashes it. The figures do reproduce: regenerating them twice gives identical bytes.
_archive: Exact-version identifier: the released header's version and the commit the archive is built from. Deliberately not the archive's own SHA-256, which cannot be recorded inside the tree it hashes. The archive is dist/bi-kappa-HEAD-00dbcce99a9d.tar.gz, 1383 entries, 2893690189 bytes, sha256 176132fcc82a5507db954b290b7b6511b4ad7ba191bef6080c2e15bf056c2a6f. tools/verify_release.py reported VERIFICATION PASSED on it: all ten checks, including strict C++11 under clang++/libc++ and g++-15/libstdc++ and the regression suite under both. No external deposit exists: publishing one is an outward-facing action and has not been authorised.
_ordering: This receipt reports two completed measurements. The analysis run that reads it changes results/analysis_report.md, because G6's own verdict is part of that report, so `make checksums`, `make verify` and `make reverify` are run once more afterwards with the receipt in place. That final pass is what certifies the tree as shipped; if it had failed, this receipt would have been withdrawn rather than the failure absorbed.
_not_supplied: dependencies_clean and baseline_comparison_resolved are deliberately absent: analyze.py measures both from the run's own record, and a receipt must not be able to overwrite a measurement the analysis can make for itself. Since commit b6cfe40 it cannot, whether or not they are present here.
_why_analyze_cannot_measure_make_verify: checksums.sha256 lists results/analysis_report.md and results/exp7_results.json. analyze.py deletes both at the start of every run -- so that a failed analysis cannot leave a stale verdict standing -- and writes them at the end. At the moment the gate's evidence is collected both are absent, and a missing file counts as a mismatch, so a self-measurement returns 1 unconditionally whatever the tree contains. Measured directly: the mismatching entries were exactly those two files. It is not an ordering problem; it is unsatisfiable, and the report carrying G6's verdict is itself hashed by the manifest, which makes it circular besides. analyze.py now verifies only the RAW manifest, which covers raw/ alone -- read by the analysis, never written by it -- and G6 requires that check to pass. `make verify` is measured by shasum, once, after the analysis has finished writing, and carried here.
